chapter_theme: The lingam of the self (ஆத்மலிங்கம்): the letters A and U, bindu as pedestal and nada as shaft, and Shakti joined with Siva make up the lingam, fixed and moving, which is Sadasiva; and the Lord who wears the moon, whom the gods seek in the eight directions, makes the devotee's mind his temple.
structure_note: Six verses (1753 to 1758) on what the lingam is made of: letters, bindu and nada, Shakti and Siva, and the tattvas mapped onto its parts. Four verses (1759 to 1762) turn to the Lord dwelling in the mind as in a temple.

1753.reading: With A first he stands as everything, with U first he stands having entered the lives; if one knows both A and U, A and U are themselves the lingam.
1753.nuance: அகாரம் and உகாரம் are the first two parts of the syllable Om, traditionally matched with Siva and Shakti, or with the Lord as all things and the Lord within souls. The verse names no subject; the reading supplies 'he'. Its first line closely echoes the Kural's first verse.

1754.reading: Bindu, which is both the support and what it supports, and nada with medha and the rest spread out above; the supporting bindu is the first pedestal, and their union is the lingam.
1754.nuance: ஆதாரம் and ஆதேயம் (support and supported) are technical terms; மேதாதி is taken as medha and the other kalas of the syllable above nada. போதா இலிங்கப் புணர்ச்சி is obscure; the plain sense is that the pedestal and the shaft together make the lingam.

1755.reading: The lingam that is Shakti and Siva is the fixed one, the lingam that is Shakti and Siva is the moving one, the lingam that is Shakti and Siva is Sadasiva, and Shakti becoming Siva is itself the fixed lingam.
1755.nuance: தாபரம் (the installed, immovable lingam) and சங்கமம் (the moving one, traditionally the devotee or the guru as a living lingam) are paired. The repetition makes one point: whatever its form, the lingam is Shakti joined with Siva.

1756.reading: One can see the light that rises straight up of itself, the place where the fifty rising toward the sky dwell; together with the golden creeper rising in the body, what rises straight up of itself is the letter A.
1756.nuance: ஐம்பது (fifty) is taken as the fifty letters, and பொற்கொடி (the golden creeper) as Shakti or kundalini. பூரேர் is obscure, perhaps a form of பூர் or a misreading; I take it as the body. The verse ends where 1753 began, with A as the lingam.

1757.reading: The lingam is where bindu and nada meet: bindu is the pedestal and nada the lingam; these two, as the supporting deities, come and perform the five acts of creation, and those are five.
1757.nuance: கருஐந்தம் is unclear; read as the five acts beginning with creation (கரு, the embryo or making). Tradition matches bindu with Shakti and nada with Siva, as the pedestal and the shaft.

1758.reading: Shakti as the good pedestal is the soul; Shakti as the good middle part is vidya; Shakti as the good lingam is the Siva tattva; and Shakti with the good soul is Sadasiva.
1758.nuance: The three parts of the installed lingam (base, middle and shaft) are matched with the three classes of tattvas, atma, vidya and Siva; கண்டம் is taken as the middle section. The last line, joining Shakti and soul as Sadasiva, is less clear.

1759.reading: When he entered my mind, my life became settled, and when he entered my mind and poured down bliss, goodness entered and sought the Lord with me, and the First One entered among his own and took me over.
1759.nuance: The subject is unstated until ஆதி (the First) in the last line. இனம்புகுந்து may mean entering the company of devotees or joining his own kind. The repeated புகுந்து (entered) carries the verse.

1760.reading: The Supreme, my Father who wears the cool moon, the support of the world, whose temple is the minds of his devotees, the Lord who abides on the heads of the gods, the one who wears the snake, has settled and dwells in my mind.
1760.nuance: Each line turns on a word ending in -பரன் (Lord): பராபரன், தராபரன், சிராபரன், அராபரன். The devotee's mind as the Lord's temple is the chapter's turn from the outer lingam to the inner one.

1761.reading: If I say 'we are not the Lord's', the foolish world will call my mind a ruined thing; the Lord who has made my mind his temple, with the snake on his red matted hair where fire and water contend, is that holy one.
1761.nuance: குரால் is obscure: it may mean something dull or faded, or a decaying thing, and the first two lines may be read differently. The image of fire and the Ganga contending on Siva's hair is a common one.

1762.reading: The gods go about the eight directions and praise him, saying 'there he stood, there he lay'; I stand and praise my Lord at all times, and he is one with me and dwells within my heart.
1762.nuance: நின்றான் கிடந்தான் (he stood, he lay) is often taken as the standing and reclining forms worshipped in temples, which the gods seek outwardly. The contrast is between seeking him abroad and finding him within; அன்று and என்று may also mean 'then' and 'always'.

links.note: Both open with A as first: the Kural uses it as a simile, as A is first of letters so the Lord is first of the world. Tirumular takes the letter literally: A and U, known rightly, are themselves the lingam.
1754 makes bindu the first pedestal and the union the lingam; 1757 names the parts plainly, bindu as pedestal and nada as lingam, and gives the pair the five acts.
Both end on the Lord dwelling in the speaker's mind; 1762 adds the contrast with the gods who seek him outwardly across the eight directions.

1752 lays the syllable Om over the lingam: ஓங்காரம் the pedestal, மகாரம் the neck, உகாரம் the inner circle, and இலிங்கம் அகாரம் the shaft itself. 1753 takes only the first two letters and says அகார உகாரம் இலிங்கம் தாமே, A as the Lord standing as all and U as the Lord within lives. Read together, 1753 explains what the A and U of 1752's diagram stand for.

1755 says the lingam that is Shakti and Siva is both தாபரம் (the installed one) and சங்கமம் (the moving one). 1857 draws the practical consequence of a moving shrine: a gift to the படமாடக் கோயில் (temple of images) does not reach the நடமாடக் கோயில் (walking temple), but a gift to the walking temple reaches the other. The pairing shows the சங்கமம் of 1755 is the living devotee to whom 1857 gives priority.

Both set the பொற்கொடி (golden creeper) inside the lingam. In 1717 the installed lingam becomes, for true worshippers, பூவகத்து உள்நின்ற பொற்கொடி; in 1756 the golden creeper rises with the light and the letters and ends as அகாரம். The shared image names Shakti as the living core of the lingam in both.

Both divide the installed lingam into the same three parts, பீடம், கண்டம் and இலிங்கம். 1752 maps them to the letters of Om; 1758 maps them to the soul, vidya and the Siva tattva, each as Shakti (சத்திநற் பீடம் தகுநல்ல ஆன்மா). The two verses give two readings of one diagram, sound and tattva.

1759 repeats மனம்புகுந்து: the Lord entered the mind, settled life and poured down இன்பம். 1804 repeats அகம்புகுந்தான்: by grace he entered the heart and made it ஆனந்தம். Both describe the Lord's entry into the inner self as the moment bliss begins, and 1804 adds that grace is the condition of that entry.

1760 calls the Lord the one whose temple is the minds of his devotees (தன்னடியார் மனக் கோயில்) and who settled in my mind. 1823 builds the whole temple inside the person: உள்ளம் பெருங்கோயில், the body the shrine, the mouth the gate, the soul the Sivalinga. 1760 states the claim in one phrase that 1823 works out part by part.

1761 speaks of the ஈசன் who made my mind his temple (என்மனம் கோயில்கொள்); 1748 says the speaker brought the bright One in and made கோயிலென் நெஞ்சம், my heart the temple. The two verses, in neighbouring lingam chapters, both move worship from the outer shrine to the heart.

2837 says the gods from Brahma and Mal on, wherever they stand, praise him as Lord (இறைவன் என்று ஏத்துவர்) while he abides. 1762 grants that the gods go round the eight directions praising him where he stood and lay, but sets against it its own constant praise and a Lord who is ஒன்றி என் உள்ளத்தின் உள்ளிருந்தான். It limits the gods' outward praise of 2837: the Lord they seek abroad is found within.

source_issues: 1756: பூரேர் in line 3 is obscure and may be corrupt.
